Chapter 17 (al-bāb al-sābiʿ ʿashar): On the occult properties of Kāf-Hāʾ- Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād and of its lordly, most holy letters [260]

Know, O truthful seeker and enamoured suitor — may God, exalted is He, guide you rightly to the alchemy (kīmiyāʾ) of everlasting felicity and the sīmiyāʾ of eternal sovereignty — that the science of the names is a noble, luminous science and a subtle, spiritual secret. Upon it the great ones among the gnostic friends of God have relied, such as the master al-Tustarī and al-Shiblī; and upon it the most excellent among the scholars firmly grounded [in knowledge] have depended, such as al-Ghazālī and al-Rāzī. It is the mother of the God-given sciences in its root, and of the designs of unveiling in its arrangement. Its reality is the holding fast to the realities of the subtle strands (raqāʾiq) of the ṣamadānī names, and the turning toward the subtleties of the gnoses of the self-disclosures of unicity that accrue to the people of the singular directednesses, which exert efficacious influence in everything receptive of them among the receptacles of contingency. And he who addresses himself to it, from among the verifiers of the gnostic scholars, is too exalted for its pillars to be shaken within the creed of the heedless ignorant.

The mirror of the secrets and the centre of the orbit of the lights, our master the Messenger of God, said: ((Among knowledge there is that which is like a thing stored up: none knows it save those who know through God; and when they speak of it, those puffed up with pride before God deny it.))
Verse
I am jealous over her, that the sun should behold her face without a veil — and the lover is jealous.

O brethren of purity, O friends of fidelity: this is the hidden pearl and the stored-up secret, the red sulphur and the brilliant ruby. Its indication is clear to the gnostics; the shell of the cryptic symbol has not veiled it from those who seek understanding; it lies concealed in the books of blindness from the heretics, and the hands of the deniers do not touch it with harm. In it are drinking-places for those who come down to the water, and its sections are indeed ascents for the wayfarers. So take it with earnest resolve, if you are given to understanding. Would you seek a witness other than the Real? Or do you not see? Only those who taste tell of what it intends; none gives expression to it save those who can expound; and none has peopled the temples of its lights save those who know. Cleave to the following of what is firmly established in it, for in it is a reminder for the worlds; and as for what is ambiguous in it — God is the best of openers.
Verse
Had the scholars beheld the hoopoe of his knowledge, they would have yearned for it with inner sights and with eyes.

And do not suppose that this luminous science and all-merciful secret has run upon the tongue and then the fingertips have traced it. Rather, every letter of it is luminous; it has not been combined with a dark letter, nor has any sublime fine point or pleasant subtlety been ordered out of it, save by an arrangement of marvellous composition and an ordering of strange disposition, after the unveiling of lofty sciences and holy understandings, and the solving of spiritual cryptic symbols, and the unlocking of the talismans of lordly treasures, and ṣamadānī self-disclosures, and unitary directednesses, and pure drinking-places, and abundant watering-places, and prodigious operations, and truthful breaths, and the understanding of the secrets of the Furqān, and luminous traces, and indications of the Throne, and Sufi expressions, and Tablet-like veiled allusions (talwīḥāt), and explicit declarations of divine bestowal, and the unveiling of the occult properties of the letter-sciences, and Indian figures, and numerical awfāq, and subtle points, odd and even, and God-given gnoses, and subtleties of opening — by which one attains to the Lordly Presence and the singular Unity, without the remoteness of wayfaring and journeying, and without weariness upon a road, or harm. So know that and verify it; understand it and examine it minutely. That is a bounty He bestows upon whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of magnificent bounty (cf. Q 62:4).

And it is of His way, mighty and majestic is He, that He gives wisdom to whom He wills (Q 2:269), and that He casts the Spirit of His command upon whom He wills of His servants (Q 40:15), and that He sends down the secret, out of His determining, upon whom He wills of His friends. So if expansion and time lend their aid, and exactitude and the season concur, and divine enabling gives help and verification keeps company; and you find rest from occupations and the sea of preoccupations, and put away dimness and confusion, muddle and hoarding, and gather the scattered mind and the absorbed thought, and snatch from the hours of your life pure times, and steal from the days of the age abiding seasons — then I have unveiled to the beauties of your spiritual understanding the brides of my luminous conception; so, in thanksgiving for the coming together at the lifting of the face-veil, from among the brides of the secrets and the precious gems of thoughts, in the ample, radiant garden and the dazzling brocaded paradise, where he who says "nor any devoted friend, nor any tender, merciful one" is filled with regret. And if the time is too straitened for that, and the hindrance bars the wayfarer, then I have brought them to you white and pure, sublime houris, fair and splendid, virginal and desirable, of Josephan form and Marian sura, of musky exhalation and Meccan opening; honoured pages, pure, purified; virgins, undefiled, of like age, dazzling, whom no thought has effaced and no remembrance has covered, whom no understanding touches and no fancy has come near — because its pearl is guarded and its secret stored up, its name kept silent and its jar sealed; its theriac is the greatest and its sulphur is red, its magnet is attracting and its ruby is procuring, its meadow is fruitful and its great tree is in blossom, its river is gushing and its bird is crying out, its lightning is gleaming and its living is copious, its light is /fol. 165v./ shining and its full moon is rising, its star is radiant and its crescent is dazzling, its fragrance is glorious and its beauty is manifest, its heaven is subtleties and its earth is gnoses, its west is secrets and its east is lights, its heart is names and its breast is sublimities, its design is wondrous and its figure is strange, its wall is verses and its fortress is recitations, its subtleties are solar and its gnoses are of unveiling, its book is hidden and its knowledge is guarded. None touches it but the purified, and none handles it but the scholars firmly grounded [in knowledge]; none understands it but the perfect friends of God, and none knows it but the pure elect; none masters it but the sages who verify, and none attains it but the excellent ones who examine minutely: And none is granted it save those who have been patient, and none is granted it save one of mighty fortune (Q 41:35).
Verse
Beauty was bewildered at her comeliness, and became like lovers, yearning for her.
And for the like of this let the workers work, and in the like of this let those who vie, vie (Q 37:61; cf. Q 83:26).

As for the benefits of the Mighty Qurʾān and the Wise Remembrance, I shall — if God, exalted is He, wills — set apart for it a healing section, a summary of the operations, sufficient, that comes near to being like the greatest theriac and the brilliant ruby.

And know — may God, exalted is He, grant success to me and to you in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that this hidden section and guarded pearl is the concealed knowledge and the sealed secret, the mighty good fortune and the ancient treasure, the healing theriac and the sufficient remedy. It is the unravelling of its cryptic symbols and the unlocking of the talismans of its treasures, the diving into the seas of its secrets and the drawing forth of its unique pearls from the depths of its abysses, and the discovery of its letter-realities and its numerical lights, its blended benefits and its odd and even occult properties, its magic-square figures and its holy litanies of remembrance, its ṣamadānī names and its spiritual secrets — besides other secrets than these, upon which none becomes informed save the few among the individuals of those firmly grounded [in knowledge], and the perfect ones among the singular ones of the gnostics. That is the bounty of God; He bestows it upon whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of magnificent bounty (Q 62:4). Some of them have contented themselves with the lexical exegesis instead of the prophetic interpretation, and with what is outward instead of what is inward; and some of them have sunk into the flood of its waves and gained the red sulphur; and some of them have waded into its depths and brought out the red ruby, the brilliant pearl and the green chrysolite; and some of them have roamed in the deeps of its expanses and gathered up the grey ambergris and the moist, freshest aloeswood; and some of them have clung to the farthest of its shores and extracted from its creatures the greatest theriac and the most fragrant musk. It is the secret which the ancients and the moderns were powerless to match, and before which those who know halted in the station of speechlessness, short of contradicting it. It is the firm rope of God and His manifest light, /fol. 166r./ His straight path and His upright way and His pre-eternal speech; the sea whose wonders do not diminish and whose marvels are not exhausted, whose furthest limit is not attained and whose exigency imagination does not reach; the discriminator between the good and the foul, the wretched and the felicitous; and the truth to which falsehood does not come from before it nor from behind it — a revelation from One All-Wise, All-Praiseworthy (Q 41:42).

And know that scholars are of four kinds: a scholar whose portion is God; a scholar whose portion from God is knowledge and gnosis; a scholar whose portion is the journey toward the hereafter; and a scholar whose portion is the knowledge of the journey toward the hereafter. The first is with [God] and through God; the second calls to God by the knowledge of God; the third calls to the hereafter; and the fourth calls to the knowledge of the hereafter — as has reached us from the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: ((Sit with the great, keep company with the sages, and question the scholars.)) And the great are those who take admonition from God through God; they are the people of understanding from God through God in His Book and in the secrets of the things He has fashioned. For between understanding and exegesis there is a difference, as God, exalted is He, has said: I shall turn away from My signs those who behave arrogantly in the earth without right (Q 7:146). Ibn ʿAbbās — may God be pleased with him — said: "I shall strip from them the understanding of the Qurʾān." And the scholars, in expressing the meanings of the Qurʾān, are of three classes: the first by exegesis, and he is the lowest of them; the second by interpretation, and he is the middling of them; the third by understanding, and he is the most majestic of them. For exegesis is by learning, study, and inquiry into the sayings of the forebears; and interpretation is by guidance, divine enabling, understanding from God, exalted is He, and judgement by intellect and analogy. And the people of understanding speak by God. He, exalted is He, has said: ((I am his tongue by which he speaks)) — to the end of the report. And Luqmān the Sage said: "The hand of God is upon the mouths of the sages, so that they utter nothing until He makes it ready for them." And Ibn ʿAbbās read And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet (Q 22:52) — "nor any muḥaddath" — and they are the people of understanding, who speak of the Qurʾān with wisdom. And it is related from one of the Companions that he said: I said, "O Messenger of God, we find in your recitation what we do not find in our own." He said: ((Because you recite outwardly, while I recite inwardly.)) And the purpose intended by that is that the nobility of the people of the inward may be known — I mean those who have understood from God, exalted is He, by the secrets of governance and the lights of admonition and the subtleties of reflection, what God intended in the inward depths of His verses, of the phases of His volitions.

And this Book is the hidden one and the treasured secret, and it is the encompassing sea from which are drawn the sciences of the ancients and of those who came after. God, exalted is He, said: We have neglected nothing in the Book (Q 6:38) — for there is no secret among the secrets but that it is [contained] in it. And it has come down from the Prophet /fol. 166v./ — God bless him and grant him peace — that he said: ((Every verse of it has an outward and an inward, up to seven inward [senses].)) And the Imām ʿAlī — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — said: Its outward is elegant and its inward is deep; its wonders do not come to an end, nor are its marvels exhausted. And it is said: there is no verse in the Qurʾān but that it has seven meanings — an outward and an inward, indications and signs, subtleties, fine points, and realities. So the outward is for the common people, the inward for the elect, the indications for the elect of the elect, the signs for the saints, the subtleties for the veracious, the fine points for the lovers, and the realities for the prophets. Then, beneath every word — nay, beneath every letter — is a sea of wisdoms, raging, possessed of a surging deep.

So when the witness among the gnostics and the truthful among the fearful recites it, he is given for every letter a mind, and for every mind a thousand understandings, and for every understanding a thousand acumens, and for every acumen a thousand lessons; and a single one of those lessons the heavens and the earth could not sustain. And it is for this that He said, exalted is He: And whoever is given wisdom has been given much good (Q 2:269) — meaning the understanding of the Qurʾān and its meanings. Some of the scholars said: every verse has sixty thousand understandings, and what remains of its understanding is yet more. And another said: the Qurʾān contains seventy-seven thousand sciences and two hundred sciences. And one of the great ones among the masters of inner sight (baṣāʾir) said: the reality of the Qurʾān rests upon the power that bears the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, from the day of their coming into being to the day of their return; and it is for that reason that among the portents of the Hour is its departure from the breasts of men and from the codices, like the folding up of the heaven and the seizing of the earth. So understand that. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.
Faṣl following upon it: On the excellence of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" and of the noble Fātiḥa

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in the understanding of His noble secrets — that whoever understands the secret of His word, exalted is He, And We send down of the Qurʾān that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers (Q 17:82) — know that in it is healing for the outward parts of bodies, just as in it is healing for the realities of hearts. And it was for this that the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — drew attention to it, saying: ((The healing of my community lies in three: a verse from the Book of God, or a cup at the hand of a cupper, or a lick of honey.)) And he said — God bless him and grant him peace: ((Whoever does not seek healing by the Qurʾān, may God, exalted is He, grant him no healing.)) And he said — God bless him and grant him peace: ((The Qurʾān — it is the remedy.)) So ponder that; and ponder and reflect upon what God, exalted is He, has deposited in this hidden Book and treasured secret, of jewels within the shells of its letters and of wonders in the deep of its sea. And here am I — if God, exalted is He, wills — about to mention, in this ample method and all-comprehending delight, something of the secrets of the Mighty Qurʾān and the Wise Remembrance.

I say — and from God comes success, and from Him unveiling and verification: One of the gnostics — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them — said: "In the name of God" /fol. 167r./ from you stands in the same relation as "Be!" stands from Him. And it has a square of majestic worth in operative deployment (taṣrīf), and this is the best of the ways of setting it down; and in it are majestic benefits: the easing of what is difficult, and the taking effect of the word among the secondary causes.

And al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī said: whoever writes "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" beautifully enters the Garden. And from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī — may God be pleased with him — he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — say: everything has a foundation; and the foundation of the books is the Qurʾān, and the foundation of the Qurʾān is the Fātiḥa, and the foundation of the Fātiḥa is "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". So when you fall ill or are indisposed, cleave to the foundation, and you will be healed, if God, exalted is He, wills.

And whoever makes remembrance of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" 787 times over a talisman, while he gazes upon this square, annuls it on the spot. And whoever recites the basmala by which God established the kingdom of Solomon — peace be upon him — and by which God established the tree of the engendered beings and manifested in it the secrets of night and day (al-malawān). And whoever draws, in the name of God, the secrets and writes them, is not burnt by fire. And in it is the secret of the Greatest Name of God; and it is the first thing that the celestial Pen traced upon the surface of the Tablet, and it is greater still. Whoever makes remembrance of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" is granted awe from the celestial and the terrestrial world. And the one who knows what God, exalted is He, has deposited in it is one whom God has granted inner discernment (iṭṭilāʿ) of the secrets of the gnoses and the sciences and of the inward aspects of their realities. So understand that. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. And know that whoever perseveres in that becomes one whose invocation is answered. Some of the scholars — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — said: whoever makes remembrance of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" 150 times, the number mentioned, and then blesses the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — 312 times, does not ask God, exalted is He, for anything without His granting it to him.
And [whoever draws "In the name of God,"] the All-Merciful, the Compassionate, in this form —
[Figure: the words of the basmala set out in the source in a two-line arrangement — upper line (bism) and (al-Raḥmān), lower line (al-Raḥīm) and (Allāh) — ]

— and along with it Sūrat al-Raḥmān, quenches the heat of fire thereby. And whoever writes it upon a slip and hangs it upon one who has toothache — and that on condition that he hang it upon the ear on that side — the pain will subside, by the leave of God, exalted is He.

And it is related from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — that he said: whoever has a need, let him fast on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday; and when it is Friday, let him purify himself /fol. 167v./ and go early to the congregational mosque, and give alms, be it little or much, from a loaf of bread down to less than that — and whatever is more is the better. Then, when he has prayed the Friday prayer, let him say: O God, I ask You by Your name "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", He of whom there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, He whom neither slumber overtakes, nor sleep (Q 2:255); and I ask You, O God, by Your name "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", who — there is no god but He, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed; He is the All-Merciful, the Compassionate (Q 59:22); I ask You by Your name whose magnificence has filled the heavens and the earth; I ask You by Your name "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", who — there is no god but He — before whom faces are humbled, and voices are hushed before the All-Merciful, so that you hear nothing but a whisper (Q 20:108), and hearts tremble in fear of Him. I ask You, O God, that You bless our master Muḥammad and the family of our master Muḥammad, and that You fulfil for me my need, which is such-and-such.
And he used to say: ((Do not teach it to your foolish ones, lest they invoke it one against another and be answered.))

And there are composed from the letters of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" nineteen names, according to the number of its letters, and they are: Allāh, al-Raḥmān (the All-Merciful), al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate), al-Rabb (the Lord), al-Salām (the Peace), al-Muʾmin (the Granter of Security), al-Muhaymin (the Overseer), al-Sattār (the Veiler), al-Ḥaqq (the Real), al-Muḥyī (the Giver of Life), al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), al-Ḥannān (the Tender), al-Mannān (the Bounteous), al-Bāriʾ (the Maker), al-Mubīn (the Evident), al-Muḥsin (the Beneficent), al-Malīʾ (the Amply Sufficient), al-Rāḥim (the Merciful), al-Ḥasīb (the Bringer to Account). And whoever sets these noble names in a square of 19 by 19 does not ask God for anything without His granting it to him; and in it is the Greatest Name of God. And its setting down ought to be within the nineteenth night, for that is the more effective.

And from the Imām ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — that he asked the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — about "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", and he said: ((It is the Greatest Name of God; and between it and the name of God, the Great, the Most Great, there is only what lies between the black of the eye and its white in nearness.)) And it is related from the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — that he said: ((In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate was sent down upon Abraham the Friend [of God], and he recited it while he was in the scale-pan of the mangonel; and God made the fire coolness and peace for him.)) And it is related of al-Awzāʿī — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — that he said: a phantom appeared to me in the night and I took fright at it, so I said, "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", and it said: you have indeed sought refuge with One who is Magnificent — and it departed from me.

And it is said that every letter of the letters of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" is the key to one of His names. So the bāʾ is the key to His name Baṣīr (the All-Seeing), and the nūn is the key to His name Nūr (the Light), and the sīn is the key to His name Samīʿ (the All-Hearing), and the mīm is the key to His name Malīk (the Sovereign), and the alif is the key to His name Allāh, and the lām is the key to His name Laṭīf (the Subtle), and the hāʾ is the key to His name Hādī (the Guide), and the rāʾ is the key to His name Razzāq (the Provider), and the ḥāʾ is the key to His name Ḥakīm (the Wise), and the mīm is the key to His name Matīn (the Firm), and the alif is the key to His name Aḥad (the Unique), and the lām is the key to His name Laṭīf also, and the rāʾ is the key to His name Raʾūf (the Ever-Gentle), and the ḥāʾ is the key to His name Ḥannān (the Tender), and the yāʾ is the key to His name Yaqḍī (He who decrees), and the mīm is the key to His name Muqaddim (the Advancer). And all these are an invocation of God, exalted is He, at the commencing of every thing. And whoever gathers the letter-square and the number-square into a single square sees of God's dealing with him what descriptions are too weak to compass; and whoever knows its worth is made independent by it of all besides it, for in it is the Greatest Name of God, exalted is He. And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills. /fol. 168r./

And were we to embark upon the spreading out of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" and of what it contains of subtleties and wonders and marvels and gnoses, the time would be too narrow for that; and moreover the divine decree does not, in this age, permit anything of the lordly secrets and the ṣamadānī traces, because it does not befit the time in which we have composed this chrysolite garden and emerald bower.

Ibn ʿAbbās — may God be pleased with them both — said: ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib took me by the hand one night and went out with me to al-Baqīʿ at the first of the night, and said: recite, O Ibn ʿAbbās. He said: so I recited "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", and he discoursed to me upon the bāʾ until the break of dawn. So understand that. And God bestows wisdom upon whom He wills, and God is All-Embracing, All-Knowing. And he said — God bless him and grant him peace: ((I was given the Fātiḥa of the Book from beneath the Throne.)) And from him — God bless him and grant him peace — that he said: ((Whoever comes to his dwelling and recites Sūrat al-Fātiḥa and al-Ikhlāṣ, God removes poverty from him and multiplies the good of his house.))
And he said — peace be upon him: ((The Fātiḥa of the Book is a healing for every ailment.))

And know that whoever understands the secret of al-ḥamd — and it is the beginning of the Mighty Book, which is the Seven Oft-Repeated — understands the secret of the praise that is in the Garden; and the praise the Book with the praise of the Garden. And ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — said: Had I wished to load seventy camels with the exegesis of the Fātiḥa, I would have done so. And one of the great ones said: In this sura there are a thousand outward occult properties and a thousand inward occult properties. And Maslama b. Qāsim b. Ibrāhīm said: The Mother of the Qurʾān (the Fātiḥa) is the head of the Qurʾān and its pillar; and in it are five names, and they are those by which God, exalted is He, ennobled this sura above the rest /fol. 168v./ of the suras. And in it is the Greatest Name of God, the Great, the Most Great, which, when He is called upon by it, He answers, and when He is asked by it, He gives. And as for these noble names, the people of knowledge of God have said that they stand at the beginning of the Preserved Tablet just as they stand at the beginning of the Mighty Qurʾān, and they are written upon the pavilions of the Throne and the Footstool. And its words point to the letters of the alphabet (ḥurūf al-muʿjam) and to the openings of the suras. And the number of its letters is 132 letters, and that is the number of his name — God bless him and grant him peace — Muḥammad. For Muḥammad is the alif of the prophets, and Aḥmad is its hamza; so Muḥammad is ʿAbd Allāh (the servant of God), and Aḥmad is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (the servant of the All-Merciful).

Laṭīfa (a subtle point). The month is twenty-nine days; and the thirtieth is at one time established and at another not established, because it stands over against āmīn, since that is a sunna and not an obligation.

And know that the wāw of conjunction in al-ḥamdu li-llāh is the pole of its circle and the axis of its revolution, since it is the numerical and literal halving (al-tanṣīf) and the halving by words; for it points to the station of sainthood (wilāya), that being the noblest of the stations, since it is the inward of prophethood. And it is composed of twenty-one letters, and there have fallen away from it these seven letters — — and these are called the letters absent from the Fātiḥa (sawāqiṭal-Fātiḥa). And it was sent down in the first Book that whoever recites a sura free of these seven letters, which are the most abased (adhlā) [reading uncertain], God makes the Fire forbidden to him. And they have been gathered together in two noble verses in Sūrat al-Anʿām. And know that the absent letters are a safeguard against the wrongdoers. So understand that. One of the gnostics said: whoever writes Sūrat al-Fātiḥa in a cup (jām) of glass with a pen of gold, in the first [hour] of the day of Friday, with musk and camphor, and effaces it with rose-water and puts it in a flask, and wipes his face with it at the time of his entering upon kings, emirs, the great ones, and viziers — he attains acceptance, love, and awe, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if it is written in a pure vessel and effaced with water, and the sick man washes his face with it, he is granted well-being, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if one much given to forgetfulness writes it in a vessel of glass and effaces it with rose-water and drinks of it for [some] days, his forgetfulness grows little, by the leave of God, exalted is He.

And in a sound report he said: whoever desires to be healed of every weakness in his sight, or of an ophthalmia that has befallen him, let him gaze upon the crescent moon on the first night; and if it is obscured from him, let him gaze on the second night and on the third. And when he sees it, let him wipe his eyes with his right hand while he recites the Mother of the Qurʾān ten times, saying the basmala at the beginning of the sura and saying āmīn at its end. Then let him recite Say: He is God, One (Q 112:1) three times, and let him say "a healing from every disease, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful" seven times, and let him say "O Lord" five times — then his sight will grow strong, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And on the authority of Anas, he said: The Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((When you lay your side upon the bed and recite the Fātiḥa of the Book and Say: He is God, One (Q 112:1), you are indeed secured from every thing except death.)) And we have imparted to you of the choice things that are with us, and have made you a gift of the rare things that we possess, of these guarded jewels and treasured rubies. /fol. 169r./ So draw to yourself what good is with your Lord and your Guarantor, and draw to yourself what you hope from Him of guidance and righteousness, by the recitation of the seven oft-repeated [verses] (al-sabʿ al-mathānī) and the Mighty Qurʾān, which you have been commanded to recite in every prayer and which it has been enjoined upon you to repeat in every rakʿa.

And the Truthful One — God's blessings and His peace be upon him — has informed you that there is not in the Torah, nor in the Gospel, nor in the Psalms the like of it. And in this there is an admonition (tanbīh) — nay, an explicit declaration — that one should multiply the recitation of it, for the benefits it comprises and the stores and singular treasures with which it has been singled out, such that, were it set down in writing, there would be in it camel-loads. So understand that; and God speaks the truth. ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd — may God be pleased with him — said: My eye ailed me, and the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said to me: ((Look into the muṣḥaf.)) Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — said: In every book there is a secret, and God's secret in the Qurʾān is in the openings of the suras. And ʿAlī — may God be pleased with him — said: Every book has a quintessence, and to the Mother of the Qurʾān belong the spelling-letters (ḥurūf al-tahajjī). And Ibn ʿAbbās was asked about Alif-Lām-Rāʾand Ḥā-Mīmand Nūn, and he said: [they are] the name al-Raḥmān (the All-Merciful) spelled out. And it is said: they are names of the Qurʾān — so said al-Suddī, al-Kalbī, and Qatāda. And it is said that they are letters by which God has sworn — so said Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿIkrima. And it is said that each letter among them indicates a name among the names of God, exalted is He, and an attribute among His attributes. Ibn ʿAbbās — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them both — said concerning Alif-Lām-Mīm: the alif is an indication that He is First; the lām, an indication that He is Laṭīf (the Subtle); and the mīm, an indication that He is Majīd (the All-Glorious). And it is said that some of these letters indicate some of the names of the Essence, and some of them the names of the Attributes. And it is said: the alif is His bounties (ālāʾ), the lām His subtlety (luṭf), and the mīm His glory (majd). And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: the alif is from Allāh, the lām from Gabriel, and the mīm from Muḥammad. And one of the gnostics mentioned that the alif means "I", the lām means "to Me", and the mīm means "from Me". And it is said: some of them indicate the names of God, and some of them indicate other than the names of God. One of the masters of the realities said that God, exalted is He, made these letters a preservation for the Qurʾān against addition and diminution; and that is what is pointed to by His words, exalted is He: Indeed We, We have sent down the Remembrance, and indeed We are its preservers (Q 15:9).

One of the scholars said that the letters that are pronounced are twenty-eight letters: half of them are the letters of light and half of them the letters of darkness. And he enumerated the letters of light, saying: they are the alif, the ḥāʾ, the ṣād, the sīn, the kāf, the ʿayn, the ṭāʾ, the hāʾ, the rāʾ, the nūn, the mīm, the qāf, the lām, and the yāʾ; and he did not enumerate the letters of darkness. And the sages used to write some of these letters upon the foreheads of the idols, so that souls might submit to them in worship, on account of matters to which they had grown accustomed. And whoever engraves these luminous letters and Furqānic secrets upon the bezel of a signet-ring of noble substance, on the first Thursday of the month of Rajab, /fol. 169v./ and wears it: if he is fearful, he is made secure; and whoever enters with it upon a sultan, he honours him and fulfils his needs and magnifies him; and whoever wipes it upon the head of an angry man, he becomes pleased with him and his anger is stilled; and whoever places it in his mouth while he is thirsty is slaked; and whoever steeps it in rainwater and drinks it, his understanding is strengthened and his memory becomes excellent; and whoever wears it while he is without employment is given free disposal (taṣarruf); and if an unmarried woman wears it, she is married; and if it is placed upon the head of one seized by a fit (maṣrūʿ), he comes to himself; and if it is wiped upon the heart of a woman in the throes of labour, she gives birth; and if it is stamped upon frankincense and one under a spell is fumigated with it, it removes his sorcery. So understand that and ponder it, for in it is the Greatest secret of God. And these are the noble names, and the wafq that goes with them, namely: Alif-Lām-Mīm, Alif-
Lām-Rāʾ, Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād, Ṭā-Hāʾ, Ṭā-Sīn, Ṭā-Sīn-Mīm, Yā-Sīn, Ṣād, Ḥā-Mīm, Qāf, Nūn. And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see.

The master Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ḥarrānī — may God, exalted is He, sanctify his spirit — said: let us confine ourselves, in the repelling of poisons, to the letters sent down at the openings of the suras. And one of the people of knowledge used to relate that he had come upon a written record [stating] that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf al-Zuhrī — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — used to write these letters upon whatever he wished to preserve of wealth and goods, and it would be preserved. And he was asked about them, and he said: they have not been set in

And the scholars — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them — when they desired a journey, one of them would write in his register the letters that stand at the openings of the suras. And there was a man among the righteous who used to travel with the letters of the alphabet (ḥurūf al-muʿjam) that stand at the openings of the suras; and he was asked about that and said: Their blessing has become manifest to me. And it is related of one of the righteous that he said: A slave-girl in his house grew restless in the night and urinated in a place where urination was not customary, and she was seized with epilepsy. By the Pen and what they set down in lines. And what she was suffering left her, and the epilepsy did not return to her. He said: And one of the great ones used to say: whoever engraves the luminous letters in a round figure of silver, with Taurus in the ascendant and the Moon within it, and keeps it by him — he will never at all be without silver. And it is not possible to declare more than that statement in this place; and God, glorified and exalted, speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. And it is related from ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib — may God, exalted is He, ennoble his face — that he said: I saw al-Khaḍir a day and a night before the encounter of Badr, and I said to him: Teach me something whereby I may be given victory over the enemies. He said: Say: "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate." O God, by the right of Alif-Lām-Mīm, and Alif-Lām-Mīm-Rāʾ, and Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād, and Alif-Lām-Mīm-Ṣād, and Alif-Lām-Mīm-Rāʾ, and Alif-Lām-Rāʾ, and Alif-Lām-Mīm-Rāʾ, and Alif-Lām-Mīm-Rāʾ, and Alif-Lām-Rāʾ, and Ṭā-Hā, and Ṭā-Sīn-Mīm, and Ṭā-Sīn-Mīm, and Yā-Sīn, and Ṣād, and Ḥā-Mīm, and Ḥā-Mīm, and Ḥā-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf, and Ḥā-Mīm, and Ḥā-Mīm, and Ḥā-Mīm, and Qāf, and Nūn: Yā Hū, O You other than whom there is no Hū, Lord forgive me and give me victory, for You are powerful over every thing. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided; and God, glorified and exalted, speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. /fol. 170v./

Thus it has come down from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him. And it is said that ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — when he made supplication would say: O al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), O al-Ṣādiq (the Truthful), O my God, grant my need in such-and-such — in a request for good and in what pertains to religion. His words Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād (Q 19:1): this is a word in which there is a treasured secret and a hidden knowledge. The kāf is from Kāfī (the Sufficient), the hāʾ from Hādī (the Guide), the yāʾ from Bāriʾ (the Maker), the ʿayn from ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), and the ṣād from Ṣādiq (the Truthful).

An all-comprehending secret, a gleaming light, and a shining pearl, by the occult properties (khawāṣṣ) of the names and the letter-secrets. It is set down on Thursday morning, in the first hour, as a fivefold figure upon a precious metal such as gold or silver, or upon gazelle parchment; and Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād is written in it five times. Then he says: O God, O al-Karīm (the Generous), O al-Hādī (the Guide), O al-Ḥayy (the Living), O al-Hādī, Bāriʾ (the Maker), O al-Ḥalīm (the Forbearing), O al-Ṣādiq (the Truthful), do for me such-and-such. And he says: This is the Greatest Name of God.

And know that if you desire acceptance in the sight of a sultan, or a judge, or a governor of affairs, and you desire that he not oppose you and that your need be granted in his presence, then take gazelle parchment likewise, and write upon it this generous wafq; suffumigate it with mastic, mahlab, and Indian aloeswood, and place the square upon your forehead beneath the turban. For you will not turn toward any need but that it is granted, by the leave of God, exalted is He; and God, exalted is He, will give you victory over your enemy. And concerning that, the Commander of the Faithful, our master ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib — may God be pleased with him — composed these verses:
Ten letters were gathered together for [their] meanings: five and five, in two forms, and they spoke.
In the two of them you see a secret. Ask a teacher, and he will show you then the meanings that have been laid open within them.
Of them is the granting of needs — the mention of that has spread abroad — and of them is the repelling of the adversary, for they have been tried and proved.
The people of knowledge have spoken of them out of their knowledge, and have said: by this secret they were singled out and given preference.
They are the guidance, and they are lofty in their excellence; and the knowledge of it is the secret that they have comprised.

So whoever inscribes this noble word upon the bezel of a signet-ring of silver on Friday, when the light prevails over the Moon, and places it upon his finger — it will be for him a light, an acceptance, an ease, a kindly regard, and a brilliance; and it is inscribed in this form.

And as for what suits this wafq among the magnificent verses, by the letter-relation and the numerical correspondence, it is in these noble verses: like water that We send down from the heaven, so that the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, and then it becomes dry stubble that the winds scatter (Q 18:45); He is God, there is no god but He, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed; He is the All-Merciful, the Compassionate (Q 59:22); the Day of the Nearing Hour, when the hearts are at the throats, choking down [their grief]; the wrongdoers have no ardent friend and no intercessor who is heeded (Q 40:18); a soul shall know what it has brought forward. And as for what agrees with them among the felicitous, blessed, noble awfāq, it is the square of Venus; for it is five by five, by the numerical relation. So we have appointed [it] for these verses, majestic in station, magnificent in proof — for Venus is a felicitous planet, consonant with the Greater Benefic in felicity and in equilibrium. By its nature it indicates growth, and increase, and felicity, and natural life; and it indicates love, and affection, and gifts, and rejoicings, and friends, and brethren, and kinsfolk. And because Venus rejoices in the fifth from the ascendant, for this reason they assigned the square of five by five to Venus. And it is written when Venus is in its exaltation or its house, and the Moon is in conjunction from the signs that agree with it; for this praiseworthy celestial relation corresponds to the noble divine relation, so that the celestial and numerical secret stands together with the divine secret — hidden, treasured, undefiled, purified, most great, greatest — and with the perfect, honoured light. Some of the scholars said: If you seek out a certain person, whether he be present in the town in which you are or absent from it, then recite these five verses sixty times, and you will find him, or find one who will direct you to him, by the power of God, glorified and exalted is He. And if a need becomes hard for you, or you are pressed for a debt, then recite these verses the said number of times, and your need will be granted with the one whom you resort to, by the leave of God, exalted is He.

Some of the eminent ones said: As for Ṭā-Hā, it is a name of Muḥammad, the lord of mankind /fol. 172v./ — and it has, of number, fourteen, and that is of the number of the days of the moon's light. And it is a most great amulet (ḥijāb).

Some of the masters of hearts said: If you are in fear of a tyrannical sultan or an overbearing wrongdoer, then take from the ground five pebbles, saying over the first,over the second,over the third,over the fourth,and over the fifth.Then you fling the first to your right while you say His word; and you fling the second to your left while you say the Real; and you fling the third behind you while you say and His is; and you fling the fourth before you while you say the kingdom (Q 6:73). Then you hold the fifth upon your head while you

— hold back your tongue, O So-and-so son of So-and-so, from So-and-so son of So-and-so, by the right of the Greatest Name, by the right of these noble names: Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād, Ḥāʾ-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf, deaf, dumb, blind, so they do not return (Q 2:18). For God, exalted is He, will bind his tongue away from you, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And it is one of the stored-up secrets.

And know — may God, exalted is He, grant success to me and to you in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that whoever sets down these noble names and subtle secrets, the fourteen, each name of them crowned with a letter of these luminous letters (and they are these names: Allāh, Laṭīf (the Subtle), Malik (the King), Ṣādiq (the Truthful), Kāfī (the Sufficient), Hādī (the Guide), ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), Muyassir (the Facilitator), Raḥmān (the All-Merciful), Ṭabīb (the Physician), Salām (the Peace), Ḥayy (the Living), Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), Nūr (the Light)), in a square upon a plate of gold, with the Sun in its exaltation or in its house — his mention is raised and his worth is exalted, his inmost secret is spread out and his breast is expanded. And it is one of the stored-up secrets. And if one who is the possessor of a truthful state multiplies the remembrance of these names, mighty in station, majestic in proof, he witnesses of the fashioning of God, blessed and exalted is He, what descriptions fall short of.

And know that if you are in a place of fear, then sit upon the ground and recite the five verses whose first is like water We sent down from the heaven, so that the herbage of the earth mingled with it, and then it became withered stubble which the winds disperse (Q 18:45), to the end of the five verses. You recite it eleven times, after you have traced a line about yourself with your finger. And that is that you make the beginning of your line by setting your finger upon the ground behind his back while you recite, until you close a circle about yourself from in front; then you complete your recitation ten times — and with the first recitation your recitation stands at eleven times. And you keep silent and speak to no one; for God will blind the sight of the people to you, and were the whole nation of the two weighty species (humankind and jinn) to come in upon you, they would not see you, by the leave of God, exalted is He.

And one of the gnostics of God, exalted is He, said: You recite these five verses sixty times upon entering before a ruler, such as a judge or another. Then, when the last of the count of the /fol. 173r./ sixty is reached, you recite,and he folds a finger of his right hand; then he saysand folds the second; then he folds the third and says;then he folds the fourth and says;then he folds the fifth finger and closes his hand and says.And likewise you do with the left hand: he recites Ḥāʾ-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf over each finger, a letter [to each], and then he closes the hand. And when he enters before the ruler, he opens his hands in his face, and he will see a wonder.

And some of the gnostics — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them — said that whoever recites these verses while seated upon the ground, and then turns his hands round behind his back and sets the index finger of the one upon the other, and begins the recitation ten times while he draws with his finger upon the ground and from behind him until he closes it before him, [saying]: "Answer, O servant-spirits of these names, by the right they have over you: hide me from the eyes of all people and from the eyes of the enemies!" — and he keeps silent and does not speak — then he is hidden from all eyes, by the leave of God, exalted is He, so long as he remains silent; and when he speaks, he becomes visible. And it has been tried, and it proved true.

And whoever recites these luminous secrets and lordly lights 256 times, and then blesses the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — 132 times: he asks no need of God, exalted is He, but that he attains it. And in it is a strange secret for kings, for the masters of leadership, and for the seekers of the lofty ranks. And no king multiplies the remembrance of it but that his kingdom becomes wide, and his subjects grow many, and his word takes effect among the secondary causes, and necks are bowed in submission to him. And in it is the hidden Greatest Name of God and His most great stored-up treasure. And this is the form of its arrangement, and it is as you see. So understand.

And know that each name of these fourteen has an operative deployment (taṣrīf) proper to it when it is set down in a square or in anything else. So understand that. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.

And know that every name has letters and numbers, and that to every number there belongs a wafq. So whoever gathers together the letters of each name and its number in a single square, the secret is unveiled to him. And whenever the number in a name is odd, the sum of its actions is by what oddness requires — so understand that. And whenever the number is even, its action lies in conjoining and the like of it, whereby its matter is made manifest — so understand. And whenever a personal name (ism dhāt) corresponds by the letter-value and the numerical value, and by its breaking and the rending open of its square, then that name is a greatest [Name] in respect of him: there is acted upon by it what is acted upon by the absolute Greatest Name. And to every laṭīfa of the names there belong verses of the Mighty Book that befit it and are proportionate to it. I say: I have arranged these names in another arrangement, and I have named them laṭāʾif (subtle points), for what we have mentioned.

The first laṭīfa: ten names — a security (amān) for the fearful, safety for those who are estranged, and the release of the imprisoned: al-Raḥmān (the All-Merciful), al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate), al-Raʾūf (the Ever-Gentle), al-ʿAfuww (the Pardoner), al-Mannān (the Bounteous), al-Karīm (the Generous), Dhū l-Ṭawl (Possessor of Bounty), Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour).

The second laṭīfa /fol. 173v./: the granting of the beautiful sciences and the subtleties of the majestic names; and they are the most majestic of the names in intimate colloquy. Whoever works with them and takes them as a litany of remembrance — there is opened for him and upon him, and he is blessed, and the sciences and bounty are made subservient to him, and an unveiling accrues to him through them. And they are six names: al-ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent), al-Ḥakīm (the Wise), al-Khabīr (the All-Aware), al-Matīn (the Firm), al-Hādī (the Guide), ʿAllām al-ghuyūb (the Knower of all things unseen).

The third laṭīfa — and it is a line of the stored-up, hidden Greatest Name: in it is the repelling of insinuating whisperings, and the overcoming of appetite, and the repelling of what is painful among grave affairs. And its time is the hours before dawn (saḥar) of every day, and it has great benefit. And they are eight names: al-Malik (the King), al-ʿAlī (the Exalted), al-ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent), al-Ghanī (the Self-Sufficient), al-Mutaʿāl (the Most Exalted), Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour), al-Muhaymin (the Overseer), al-Kabīr (the Great).

The fourth laṭīfa: for awe and for the great wars. In it is a portion of the hidden Greatest Name, and by it all creatures are acted upon — especially for the scattering of what is gathered and the gathering of what is scattered. Whoever perseveres in them, God lifts from him every painful thing; and whoever is wronged, God grants him victory over [his wronger]. And it is fitting that it be recited in the presence of tyrants, and of the great ones of creation, and of the overbearing among kings: they continue unharmed, and he continues honoured; and there are made subservient to him the eight [kinds of] beasts and the hard hearts. And they are ten names: al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty), al-Qawī (the Strong), al-Qādir (the Powerful), Dhū l-Quwwa (Possessor of Strength), al-Matīn (the Firm), al-Muqtadir (the Omnipotent), al-Jabbār (the Compeller), al-Mutakabbir (the Supremely Great), al-Shadīd (the Severe), al-Qādir (the Powerful).

The fifth laṭīfa: in it is the Greatest Name of God, that by which, when He is invoked, He answers, and by which, when He is asked, He gives; and the people of the unveilings have an acquaintance with it. And it is among the greatest of the litanies of remembrance. And no one persists in the remembrance of them but that unveiling is granted him, and the object of request is made easy for him, and he is provided with what he desires in weighty matters. So whoever recites them at the middle of the night witnesses wonders; and perseverance in them opens the secrets of the things of the Dominion. And in them is the preservation of the soul and the body from what is painful, and the subduing of enemies. And they are among the hidden litanies of remembrance: no one persists in the remembrance of them but that he sees something of the affairs of the upper world, and looks upon secrets of the world of being, and there is made subservient to him [what is] in every world. And they are the perfect words. And they are ten names: al-Muḥīṭ (the All-Encompassing), al-ʿĀlim (the Knower), al-Rabb (the Lord), al-Shahīd (the Witness), al-Ḥasīb (the Bringer to Account), al-Faʿʿāl (the Doer of what He wills), al-Khallāq (the Creator of all), al-Bāriʾ (the Maker), al-Muṣawwir (the Shaper).

The sixth laṭīfa: it has an occult property in the preservation of the sciences and for those who give legal responsa; and for the people of gnosis there is in it intimate colloquy and litanies of remembrance, and the purifying of the hearts of the ascetics from the weariness of the soul. And in it, for the gladdening of the soul, are the channels of the divine determining. And they are ten names: al-Badīʿ (the Wondrous Originator), al-Bāṭin (the Hidden), al-Ḥafīẓ (the Preserver), al-Kāmil (the Complete), al-Mubdiʾ (the Initiator), al-Muʿīd (the Restorer), al-Mughīth (the Succourer), al-Majīd (the All-Glorious), al-Ṣādiq (the Truthful), al-Wāsiʿ (the All-Embracing).
The laṭīfa

The seventh laṭīfa: it is among the mightiest of the litanies of remembrance, and unveiling befalls the one who makes remembrance with it. /fol. 174r./ In it is the Greatest Name of God. Whoever keeps constantly to it has [things] unveiled to him; at the middles of the nights he witnesses wonders. And if he knows the manner of its divisions, he is made rich by it with everlasting riches, and it becomes for him a means of nearness to the Real. And they are ten names: al-Wahhāb (the Bestower), al-Bāsiṭ (the Expander), al-Ḥayy (the Living), al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), al-Nūr (the Light), al-Fattāḥ (the Opener), al-Baṣīr (the All-Seeing), al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty), al-Wadūd (the Loving), al-Wāsiʿ (the All-Embracing).

The eighth laṭīfa: it has a swift efficacious influence for one who seeks the secondary causes, and for the making of blessings to take root; and it brings back for ever what has strayed away of them. Its benefit is the making easy of what is hard among the secondary causes and among the causes of provision; and faces turn toward him, and blessing comes of earning; and it makes subservient to him everyone of whom he asks a need. And it is suitable for the people of beginnings, for it is magnificent. And they are nine names: al-Tawwāb (the Ever-Relenting), al-Ghāfir (the Forgiver), al-Ḥasīb (the Bringer to Account), al-Wakīl (the Trustee), al-Kāfī (the Sufficient), al-Razzāq (the Provider), al-Salām (the Peace), al-Muʾmin (the Granter of Security), al-Sarīʿ (the Swift).

The ninth laṭīfa: it is fifteen names, [and it lies] in the knowledge of the kingdom and the Dominion, and the secret of what is decreed, and the loci where the effusion falls in the celestial and the terrestrial world. Whoever perseveres in the remembrance of them upon an empty stomach beholds in himself loftiness of aspiration, and a thrusting toward the inward matters such as he had not known of himself; and souls turn toward him, and hearts are acted upon for him with a subtle receptivity (infiʿāl). And if he is fearful, he is made secure, and the one who wrongs him is kept from him. And these are the names: al-Muḥyī (the Giver of Life), al-Mumīt (the Bringer of Death), al-Qābiḍ (the Constrictor), al-Bāʿith (the Raiser of the dead), al-Wārith (the Inheritor), al-Shāfī (the Healer), al-Barr (the Benign), al-Awwal (the First), al-Ākhir (the Last), al-Ẓāhir (the Manifest), al-Bāṭin (the Hidden), al-Quddūs (the All-Holy) — He did not beget and was not begotten, and to Him none is equal (Q 112:3–4).

And know that these laṭāʾif are swift in efficacious influence and prosperous in acceptance; for what is recommended is that each laṭīfa be engraved upon a signet-ring of gold — the two bodies of gold and the remainder of silver, that is to say the bezel and the ring — or else that it be upon the bezel of a signet-ring of a single body. Then, when he wishes to make remembrance with one of these laṭāʾif, let him seal with its signet and make remembrance of it; for they are swift of response.

His words, glorified and exalted is He: And if a prompting from Satan should prompt you, then seek refuge with God — up to His words — and at once they are seeing (Q 7:200–201). These verses are for obsessive whispering (waswasa), for fear and terror, for the soul's inner talk, for imaginings, and for trembling. So whoever has anything of that befall him, let him write them with rose-water and saffron on a Friday upon seven leaves at sunrise, and let him swallow one leaf each day, drinking upon it a draught of water; for he will be healed, if God, exalted is He, wills. I say: it is related in the Ṣaḥīḥof al-Bukhārī and in that of Muslim, from Abū Hurayra — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((Satan comes to one of you and says, "Who created such-and-such?" — until he says, "Who created your Lord?" So when he reaches that, /fol. 174v./ let him seek refuge with God and with His prophet.)) And in [another] transmission in the Ṣaḥīḥ: ((People will not cease questioning one another until it is said, "This is God's creating — so who created God?" Whoever finds that [in himself], let him say: I have believed in God and in His Messenger.)) And al-Tirmidhī related from ʿĀʾisha — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with her — who said: The Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((Whoever finds anything of this obsessive whispering, let him say, "We have believed in God and in His Messenger," three times; for that will make it depart from him.)) And Muslim related from ʿUthmān b. Abī l-ʿĀṣ, who said: I said, "O Messenger of God, Satan has come between me and my prayer and my recitation, confusing it upon me." So the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((That is a satan called Khinzab. When you sense him, seek refuge with God from him and spit dryly to your left three times.)) So I did so, and God made him depart from me. The master Muḥyī l-Dīn al-Nawawī said in his commentary on Muslim: Khinzab — with a dotted khāʾ, then a vowelless nūn, then a zāy with fatḥa, then a bāʾ with a single dot. And the scholars have differed over the vowelling of the khāʾ: some of them give it fatḥa and some of them kasra, and these two are the well-known [readings]; and some of them give it ḍamma, which Ibn al-Athīr reported in Nihāyat al-gharīb. And what is [best] known is the fatḥa and the kasra.

And it is related from Abū Dāwūd, from Ibn Zumayl, who said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās, "There is something I find within myself." He said, "What is it?" I said, "By God, I will not utter it." He said, "Is it something of doubt?" — and he laughed. And he said: No one escaped it until God, exalted is He, sent down And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you (Q 10:94) — the verse. Then he said to me: ((When you find something within yourself, say: He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knower of all things (Q 57:3).)) Some of the scholars have said: it is recommended to say "There is no god but God" — so whoever is afflicted with obsessive whispering in the ablution, in the prayer, and the like [should say it]; for Satan, when he hears the litany of remembrance, slinks away, that is, he draws back and withdraws. "There is no god but God" is the head of remembrance, and for that reason the eminent masters among the choicest of the community chose, for the way of the wayfarers and for the disciplining of the aspirants, the saying "There is no god but God," for the sake of the spiritual retreat (khalwa); and they commanded them to persevere in it. And they said: the most beneficial remedy for repelling obsessive whispering is turning toward the remembrance of God, exalted is He, and multiplying it. The majestic master Aḥmad b. al-Khwārizmī said: I complained of obsessive whispering to Sulaymān al-Dārānī — may God be pleased with him — and he said: If you wish it to be cut off from you, then at whatever time you sense it, rejoice; for when you rejoice at it, it is cut off from you, since there is nothing more hateful to Satan than the joy of the believer. But if you grieve over it, he increases it upon you. And the master Muḥyī l-Dīn said: This supports what some of the scholars have said — that obsessive whispering afflicts only one whose faith is complete; for the thief does not make for a ruined house.

From Abū l-Dardāʾ: whoever says seven times every day But if they turn away, then say: God suffices me; there is no god but He. Upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne (Q 9:129) /fol. 175r./ — God, exalted is He, suffices him in whatever concerns him of the affair of his world and of his hereafter, whether he be truthful or lying. And in [another] transmission: ((He shall not die by collapse, nor by drowning, nor by burning, nor be harmed by iron.)) And from al-Layth b. Saʿd, from Abū Maʿshar: a man's thigh was broken, and one came to him and said to him: Put your hand where you find your pain, and say But if they turn away, then say: God suffices me; there is no god but He. Upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne (Q 9:129). And his thigh became sound, and he was cured. And among the occult properties of this verse: whoever writes it and hangs it upon himself does not stand before a ruler but that he fulfils his need, by the leave of God, mighty and majestic is He.
Faṣl: On the inclining and joining together of hearts

You write seven times Yā Allāh (O God), and seven times Yā Raḥmān (O All-Merciful), and seven times Yā Raḥīm (O Compassionate). Then you write: O God, soften the heart of So-and-so toward So-and-so, and place with him mercy, gentleness, affection, tenderness, and acceptance. But if they turn away, then say: God suffices me; there is no god but He. Upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne (Q 9:129). And when Abraham said: My Lord, show me how You bring the dead to life. He said: Do you not believe? He said: Yes indeed — up to His words — Mighty, Wise (Q 2:260). And likewise let So-and-so come to So-and-so, submissive and abased. So We have stripped from you your covering, and your sight this day is keen (Q 50:22). You write it with saffron, pepper, and lead, and you circle with it about the head of whomever you wish, seven times, in whatever way is made easy for you, whether while he sleeps or while he is awake — [this] with one who is close at hand, such as a husband and wife or the like of them. And if he be one whose head you cannot reach, then circle it at a distance from him, where you can see him and he cannot see you, while you make the takbīr once at every circuit, saying: God is greatest, God is greatest — seven takbīrs. And you carry it with you; for God, exalted is He, has mercy upon him, and he follows you and is led obediently to you. And God is the granter of success. ((And deeds are only by intentions, and to every matter belongs only what was intended.)) You write it on a Thursday at sunrise, in his protective amulet.
Faṣl

And this is the swift Name: ahl ahlā ahlah, the Essence, the Spirit, and the Knowledge. Yā Barr (O Benign), Yā Waṣūl (O Ever-Joining): join So-and-so to So-and-so, and join affection between the two of them. Bahlaṭīf shalīṭīʿ asmāṭūn aṭūn hakash barqash hayūrash bahlahalyūh al-arkiyāṣhayūrash yārūsh al-shaq al-shaqūm mahrāqash yashlaḥaṭ yashlīyūsh baʿzanfūsh qalshāqūm ʿalshāqash mahrāqash. Answer, O helpers, by the treasured, concealed Name! Answer, O Sālim! Answer, O Maymūn! You write it on a Wednesday with the water of clove-basil, with saffron, and with good rose-water, upon leaves of reed, together with the name of whomever you wish; and you hang it up in the wind, and suffumigate it with good male frankincense.

And let your midday meal, during the days of the service, be bread and oil — or one time and another. You go into retreat for seven days in a place empty /fol. 175v./ of people, and you keep devotional seclusion in a sound state, and you fast your day and break your fast upon what I have mentioned, short of satiety; and you make remembrance of them after the five prayers, and you deploy them operatively in whatever you wish — the falling sickness caused by the companion-spirit (qarīn), the bringing of one who is absent, the turning of paper (kāghad) into gold and silver, and everything you desire. So through it be one whose lot is envied, and do not disclose your secret to anyone: you will attain your hope, and your desire will be obtained to good effect. And this is the Seal of Obedience, and in it are the swift Name and the lofty ascendant. It is written in one thousand one hundred and eighty names, and that is what you write the ascendant in. And this number is gathered in three letters, and in it there is preposing and postposing — so understand; for walls have ears, and that a mindful ear might keep it in mind (Q 69:12). And this is the form of the seal.

Faṣl

You write these names in the pillow of two spouses who hate one another — and they are the names of the mother of Moses, peace be upon him — on a Friday, when the imam sits upon the pulpit and the first call to prayer is begun, with saffron, with good rose-water, with good cloves, and with yellow male frankincense.

— [male frankincense] that is good, powdered, and with cloves rubbed fine, in sweet-scented Naṣībī rose-water. Then fold up the writing and anoint it with fine, choice ghāliya-perfume; and you put the writing inside the pillow upon which the two of them sleep, for they will love one another, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And this is what you write: Ṭasūm Ṭasūm ʿAyshūm ʿAyshūm ʿAlūm ʿAlūm Kalūm Kalūm Ṣayūm Ṣayūm Qayyūm Qayyūm Dayūm Dayūm. Glory be to Him by whose remembrance hearts are set at rest! Be at rest, O heart of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], for the love of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]. O God, set right [what is] between So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] and So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], as You set right [what was] between Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — and his helpers (anṣār). O God, O You who caused the love of Joseph to enter into the heart of Zulaykhā; O You who caused the love of Moses to enter into the heart of Āsiya bint Muzāḥim; and O You who caused the love of Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — to enter into the heart of Khadīja bint Khuwaylid and of ʿĀʾisha bint Abī Bakr: cause the love of such-and-such to enter into the heart of such-and-such, as You caused the night to enter into the day and the day into the night, and the male into the female. Had you spent all that is in the earth, you could not have joined their hearts in affection; but God joined them in affection. Truly He is Mighty, Wise (Q 8:63). And there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. And if you wish, you write it after the rising of the sun on a Friday.
Faṣl

And among them also: Dhū l-Nūn ibn Ibrāhīm al-Miṣrī — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — was asked /fol. 176r./ about the names of the mother of Moses, peace be upon him. And he said: The transmissions we have are many, but that whose trial has been verified with us is this: that when you wish to employ them, you fast seven days and speak to no one; and you give alms each day to three poor men; and each day you suffumigate your place of prayer, morning and evening, with male frankincense and aloeswood; and you recite the names by number, after each prayer, seven times. And when that has been completed for you, you recite it within yourself; and you shall not invoke over a lock, nor over a chain, nor over a bolt, but that it opens for you swifter than the blink of an eye, by the leave of God, exalted and hallowed is He. And it is this. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Lord of Hulbā bint Raghbā, the believing woman, the truthful, the mother of Moses — peace be upon him — by God, the Mighty, the Wise, Haliyā, the Supremely Great, the Great, the Overseer, the Magnificent, by whom the layers [of heaven] are opened, and by whom the horizons were made to shine, and by whom the hardest things were opened: open this lock, or this fetter! And if you wish, you say: So-and-so son of So-and-so, with the love of So-and-so son of So-and-so, by God, the Mighty, the Supremely Great, the Great, the Overseer, the Magnificent. And it is said in another transmission that the names of the mother of Moses — peace be upon him — which loose locks and fetters and other things than that, are these: Ṭasūm Ṭasūm Ayūm Ayūm Ḥayūm Ḥayūm Qayyūm Qayyūm Dayūm Dayūm. O God, O You who opened the sky with abundant rain: open such-and-such — and you make mention of whatever you intend of locks and fetters, or of hearts — truly You are powerful over everything.

O God, Ashbīh Ashbīh wa-Shabīh wa-Zaydūḥwa-Badīḥwa-Ṭāḥūl wa-Muḥīl lah wa-Takāmad wa-Salām wa-Māyūḥā wa-Muḥallalūt wa-Umm Aḥrāh Junūduhā Ḥābūrah Būrah Badīḥā wa-Ḥānīt Ḥanūnah Mardūdah Qāl Maj Maʿaj Ṭafaf Lafaf Kafaf Sahaf Faʿīl Yālīṭā wa-Ṭāyā Dabā Lakarīrah — [I adjure you] that you assuredly take charge, and answer, and obey God and His Messenger and His power and His authority. Open this lock! And if it be of iron, make it fly away; and if it be of brass or of copper or of wood, then break it, by the right of these names that are upon you. And if you wish: open the heart of such-and-such with love and affection toward such-and-such. Completed with the help of God, exalted is He.
Faṣl: In which I mention the seal of Solomon — peace be upon him

Know that whoever seals with it, God, exalted is He, preserves him — inasmuch as he preserves himself from disobedience, and is pure, clean of garment, silent of tongue, God-fearing before God, mighty and majestic is He — with swiftness of response. And it is the Seal of Obedience: none touches it save one who is mighty. Wahb b. Munabbih — may God be pleased with him — said: The seal of Solomon — peace be upon him — was upon four corners; above each corner there was written: on the right side, "I am God, I have never ceased to be"; and on the left side, "I am God, the Living, the Self-Subsisting"; and on the third side, "I am God, the Mighty; there is no mighty one but Me, and mighty is he whom I have clothed with My seal"; and on the fourth there was written /fol. 176v./ the Throne Verse, encircled by "Muḥammad is the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace."
Faṣl of the same

And it is said that these names, which were upon the seal of Solomon — peace be upon him — are these: There is no god but God, alone, having no partner. I am God: I am alone in the kingship and the authority. Īl Īl Īl. I am God: I have made Myself mighty with might and with power. Yāh Yāh Yāh. I am God, Living, Self-Subsisting; I do not sleep. Ayh Ayh Ayh. I am God, All-Aware, Powerful; everything has obeyed Me. Anūkh Anūkh Anūkh. I am God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Dāʿūj Fayʿūj Māʿūj. There is no god but God: [it is] My fortress — whoever enters it is secure from My torment. I have fortified myself with the names of this seal, and with the Possessor of might and of omnipotence; and I have taken refuge from my enemies with the Possessor of power and of strength and of the Dominion; and I have committed my affair to the Living who does not die; and I have thrust back whoever intended harm against me — with no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. God is our sufficiency, and excellent is the Guardian (Q 3:173). Say: O God, Master of all Dominion — to His words — without reckoning (Q 3:26–27).
Faṣl

And it is mentioned that these names were upon the collar of the robe (julla) of Solomon — peace be upon him — and that they are of mighty blessing, proper to kingship and authority. And they are: Īl Īl Īl. I am God: I am alone in the might and the strength and the power. Yāh Yāh Yāh. I am God, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, a Self-Subsisting one who does not sleep. Ah Ah Ah. I am God, the One, the All-Subduing, Living, Powerful; nothing of mine is lost. Anūkh Anūkh Anūkh. I am God, the Mighty; there is no mighty one but Me; I have made Myself mighty above the like and the equal. Dāʿūj Fayʿūj Dāʿūj. There is no god but God: a fortress — whoever enters it is secure from My torment. I have fortified myself with the Possessor of might and of the Dominion, and I have taken refuge with the Possessor of strength and of omnipotence, and I have relied upon the Living who does not die; and I have thrust back whoever cast at me and intended for me evil, or guile, or deception, or a false invocation — with no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. And I have taken refuge with God, and I have relied upon God, and upon His names, the treasured, the concealed, the generous, the majestic. Ah Ah Ah Lūʿālīh Dāyūm Ṭasūm Qayyūm

Dayūm; and by the right of Ḥā-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf, and by the right of Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād, and by the right of the Ḥawāmīm and the generous verses that are in them: I have veiled myself with them, and with the might of God by which He created Muḥammad, God bless him and grant him peace.
Faṣl

And it is related concerning these names — and they are among the names of the shining light whose light overcame every light — that Solomon son of David, upon him be blessing and peace, when he sat in his session, the jinn would tremble before him in awe and in fear of these names. And they are: There is no god but God; the command is wholly God's; and there is no victor that overcomes God. Light, light, light! Glory be to Him whose light has overcome every light! And there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād. Jahlās Wāḥiṣlī Waraḥsamā Kasṭasṭī /fol. 177r./ MaṭaṭhaṭaṭHaṭāhaṭHayf. Answer! There is no god but God. It has shone and blazed forth. Ṭūb Ṭūb, All-Glorified, All-Glorified, Hayṭūb Hayṭūb, All-Holy, All-Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit! Upon the Throne He is established, and over the kingship He has taken hold, and to Him belong the Most Beautiful Names. There is none to repel what He has decreed, and none to withhold what He has given. He does in His kingdom what He wills, and He judges among His creatures as He wishes; and He is powerful over everything. You write [them] upon gazelle parchment, or upon the parchment of a lamb (ʿabūr), with musk and saffron; and you suffumigate them with the sweetest incense.

And this chapter is operatively deployed in seventy-one matters: for going in before sultans; for standing before rulers, and prisoners, and the bewitched; and for empty roads; and for hard labour in childbirth, and fever, and the divorced woman, and a blow (laṭma); and for love between a man and his wife, and brothers, and sisters, and mothers; and for selling and buying. And its operative deployment is manifold. So know its worth, and guard it with all your effort, and beware of disobedience — for in it is the name of God, the Magnificent, the Greatest. And they are the names whose mention has gone before, and the seals that were upon the collar of Solomon — peace be upon him.

And it is related from al-Ḥajarī, from Kaʿb al-Aḥbār — may God be pleased with him — that he said: Upon the carpet of Solomon — peace be upon him — were names that struck the jinn senseless, and by which they were torn apart, and by which he was obeyed by them, and by which he tormented them. And in the middle of the carpet were four Hebrew names, locked; on account of which the jinn and the satans were obedient, not disobeying him for the blink of an eye. And they were the helpers of the carpet, charged with the raising of it: four ʿifrīts, who were among the greatest of the viziers of Solomon — peace be upon him — from among the jinn. And the viziers of Solomon from among mankind were three hundred, the greatest of them being Āṣaf b. Barakhyā, and three hundred from among the jinn, the greatest of them these four: Ẓamriyāṭ, Ṣanʿīq, Hadliyāj, and Shūghāl. And these names have a mighty obedience over the jinn and the satans. So know their worth and their excellence, and do not squander them, and do not disclose them to anyone of God's creatures, exalted is He. And beware of commanding the helpers to be made subservient; rather say to them: O company of the four helpers and the honoured viziers, [I adjure you] that you assuredly command one who will fulfil my need and act freely in what pleases me, by the right of the prophet of God, Solomon, and by the right of Him who said: An ʿifrīt of the jinn said: I will bring it to you before you rise from your place; and truly I am strong and trustworthy for it (Q 27:39); It is from Solomon, and it is: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Do not exalt yourselves above me, but come to me in submission (Q 27:30–31) — hastening, with tranquillity and with gravity.

And you write each name upon its day, while you are pure of body, of garment and of place, and in the hour of its brilliant star (durrī); and you suffumigate them with the sweetest and finest incense; and you take its star-reading by night beneath the stars, with Sūrat Yā-Sīn and Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion (Q 67:1). And to these /fol. 177v./ four names belong four days. The first, and it is for the day of Sunday, and its first hour, at the rising of the sun; and its helper is Ḍamriyāṭthe ʿifrīt, and the lord of the hour is al-Mudhhab al-Kibrīt; and this is its name: Hashṭashlahakūsh — nine letters. And the second is for the day of Tuesday, and its first hour; and its helper is Shūghāl the ʿifrīt, and the lord of…

— the hour is al-Aḥmar Abū l-Tawābiʿ, and this is its name: Kashkashlīʿūsh — nine letters. The third is for the day of Wednesday, and its first hour; and its servant is Dībāj the ʿifrīt, and the lord of the hour is Barqān, and its brilliant star (durrī) is ʿUṭārid (Mercury); and this is its name: Baḥshahshalṭūsh — nine letters. And the fourth is for the day of Saturday, and its first hour; and its helper is Ṣanʿīq the ʿifrīt, and the lord of the hour is Maymūn Abū Nūkh; and this is its name: Shaṭlaṭaṭlakūsh — nine letters. And these nine letters belong to each name only because the nine is the utmost of number and the strongest of it, and to it the numbers come to their end. So understand that. And this is the form of the seal.
