And it is related that this is its conjuration (ʿazīma) and the utterance upon which it stands; and it is: O God, O al-Qawī (the Strong) — there is no strong one but You. O God, O God, O God. O Creator of the night and the day, O Sender of the clouds and the winds, O Lord of lords, O Emancipator of necks, Powerful over whatsoever He wills and desires, from whom nothing among things is hidden, who fears no punishment and hopes for no reward, the Subduer by His power, the Compassionate by His mercy: I have asked you by the signs of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate, the Lord of the trustworthy Spirit, Gabriel; and of the mighty, sublime angel, Mīkāʾīl; and of the angel charged with the blast [of the Trumpet], Isrāfīl; and of the dread angel from whom hearts tremble, ʿAzrāʾīl; and of the bearers of the Throne, all of them — that you assuredly command one who will fulfil my need and act freely in what pleases me, by the right of the prophet of God, Solomon — peace be upon him — by the right of Him who said: Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission? An ʿifrīt of the jinn said — to His saying — trustworthy (Q 27:38–39); It is from Solomon — to His saying — in submission (Q 27:30–31). O God, I ask You by these spiritual spirits, honoured in Your sight, that You make subservient to me the four ʿifrīts, by Your power /fol. 178r./ and Your majesty: Bahshahash Mahshahash Faṭūsh Layhūsh Kashkash Layūsh ShakhshalūṭShaḥshaṭKhajaj Khajaj. Answer, and take charge, and do what you are commanded.

I say: and among the occult properties of the majestic benefits is His word, exalted is He: And he said: Embark in it; in the name of God is its sailing and its anchoring. Truly my Lord is Forgiving, Compassionate (Q 11:41). This verse is for whoever has a ship, and it is at sea, and he desires its safety from the deeps of the sea: let him engrave that upon a plank of teak wood and nail it at the prow of the ship — and in [another] copy: at the stern of the ship — for that will be for it a protective charm and a safeguard, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī, who said: The Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((A security for my community against drowning, when they ride in the ship, is that [they say]: In the name of God is its sailing and its anchoring. Truly my Lord is Forgiving, Compassionate (Q 11:41); And they have not esteemed God with the esteem that is His due (Q 39:67), the verse.)) Thus it stands in some of the copies: "when they ride"; and it does not say "" ,"…in the ship, that they say: And he said: Embark in it; in the name of God is its sailing and its anchoring. Truly my Lord is Forgiving, Compassionate". You say: /fol. 178v./ And they have not esteemed God with the esteem that is His due (Q 39:67), the verse. And he stands in the rear parts and faces the prow and gestures to the right and to the left; then he says: Abū Bakr and ʿUmar — and he gestures toward the stern; then he says: ʿUthmān > and ʿAlī < — and he gestures toward the prow; then he says: ʿAlī; then he says: In the name of God. In the name of God we have named; by Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād we have been sufficed, and by Ḥā-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf we have been protected. And God is encompassing them from behind; nay, it is a majestic Qurʾān, upon a preserved Tablet (Q 85:20–22). Ibn ʿAbbās said to his companions: Whoever says, when he mounts his riding-beast or his conveyance: In the name of God, the King. And they have not esteemed God with the esteem that is His due, and the whole earth shall be His handful on the Day of Resurrection — to His saying — above what they associate (Q 39:67); And he said: Embark in it; in the name of God is its sailing and its anchoring. Truly my Lord is Forgiving, Compassionate (Q 11:41) — then he turned to his companions and said: If it comes to harm or sinks, then his intention is upon me. Ibn Shabak said: I came to the shore of Baḥr Barsh, and I found upon the shore twenty-two ships laden with grain. So I went aboard one of them, and said the words and recited the verses, and the ships ran on with a fair wind until a third of the night; then the wind blew violently and the waves rose high, and none reached a shore — for there was none other than the ship I was in — and of the rest of them no trace was seen.

And from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar, that he said: A security against drowning and shipwreck for whoever rides the sea is that he say: In the name of God, the King, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. And they have not esteemed God with the esteem that is His due (Q 39:67), the verse. And he said: Embark in it; in the name of God is its sailing and its anchoring. Truly my Lord is Forgiving, Compassionate (Q 11:41). And when you and those with you are settled upon the ship, say: Praise be to God, who has delivered us from the wrongdoing people (Q 23:28). Truly God upholds the heavens and the earth, that they should not pass away (Q 35:41) — the verse, to its end. And God is encompassing them from behind (Q 85:20), the verse. And in a report from Ibn ʿAbbās — may God be pleased with them both — that he said: Whoever says, when he rides the sea: In the name of God, the King. Kingship belongs to God. O You for whom the seven heavens are in fear, and the seven earths in trembling, and the lofty mountains in humility, and the surging seas in submission: guard me — You are the best guardian, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful. And they have not esteemed God with the esteem that is His due — to His saying, glorified and exalted is He — above what they associate (Q 39:67).
